newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to apologize to medical research victims.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to apologize to medical research victims.

text.p: President Clinton is to formally apologise on Friday to black men whose syphilis went untreated for decades as part of a federal study.
Five of the eight living survivors of the U.S. Public Health Service study, which began in Tuskegee, Alabama, in 1932 and lasted for 40 years, will attend the White House ceremony.
Herman Shaw, 94, who was part of the group, will speak at the event.
Clinton's apology will be beamed to Tuskegee on satellite.
The government medical experiment involved 400 black men who were left untreated for syphilis even though penicillin became widely avalable during the study.
Survivors have been financially compensated, but there has never been a government apology.

"It's something that the victims and their families and the residents of Macon County, Alabama, will appreciate and have indeed sought. And the president thinks it's most warranted to give," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

The spokesman said Clinton will also offer some specific ideas "on things that we can do to address in general the question of proper funding and proper accountability for federally funded medical research."

Clinton's apology is not unprecedented. He previously expressed regret to Americans who unknowingly served as guinea pigs in government radiation experiments that took place years before he became president.
